messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: control-plane API /v1/auth responding 502/504 from multiple regions — error rate spike > 7% (5m window). Paging: @sam-oncall :rotating_light:
sam-oncall: acked, jumping in. pulling logs now. which customer impact?
ryan-eng-runtime: seeing elevated org-lookup latencies from control-plane to org-service; stacktrace shows timeouts to billing-lookup. same across us-east/us-west.
maria-cs: support already seeing 5 customer-reported errors in last 10m, 2 on Dedicated tenants. escalating to account owners.
tina-sre: I'm on traces. Sampling shows the upstream call to billing-lookup DB sits at ~3s then times out at 4s, causing gateway to return 502.
sam-oncall: good data. mitigation options: 1) enable aggressive circuit-breaker to short-circuit to cached org results; 2) rollback recent config deploy that touched billing connection pool; 3) scale billing-lookup horizontally. any quick wins?
ryan-eng-runtime: we pushed a config tweak 18m ago that reduced DB pool from 200->50 (attempted to reduce fds). that aligns with spike. rolling it back now.
sam-oncall: +1 rollback. doing canary rollback on control-plane config. will post status.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback job started (config:control-plane:2026-03-15T10:12) -> revert to control-plane-config:v2026-03-14. ETA ~120s.
ryan-eng-runtime: while rollback runs, I pushed a temporary route rule on gateway to send org-lookup to warm cache path: route /v1/org -> control-plane-cache-primed alias. small risk but lowers load.
tina-sre: adding CB rule: set failureThreshold=3, openPeriod=30s for billing-lookup target. applied.
sam-oncall: rollback complete. observability: error rate dropping from 7% -> 3.5% over 90s. seeing fewer timeouts in traces.
maria-cs: notifying impacted customers: "We're investigating higher error rates for auth/organization lookups. We've applied mitigations; we'll update in 30 minutes." sending now. cc @support-leads
ryan-eng-runtime: follow-up: found the config change also lowered maxIdleConns in the billing client. that combined with sudden traffic spike caused DB pool exhaustion. root cause = config rollback required.
sam-oncall: telemetry confirms p99 latency back to baseline ~120ms. error budget consumption halting.
tina-sre: saving logs and traces to the incident channel. attaching key traces and query samples.
sam-oncall: action items: 1) ry an to file PR that reverts the pool change + add safer default and a rollout gate, 2) tina to run capacity runbook for billing-db, 3) maria to publish customer update and open PSR if any customer SLA blips. I'll hand off at 11:00 to next oncall.
ryan-eng-runtime: filing PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/control-plane/pull/4827 (revert: conn-pool-change + unit tests). will request review from @tina-sre.
maria-cs: customer update posted to status.redwood.com and sent to affected accounts. copying here: "Mitigation applied: configuration rollback and circuit-breaker. Root cause investigated: pool sizing regression. We will follow up with a timeline for permanent fix."
devops-bot: pagerlog: incident 2310001234 created, severity: high, pages: 3.
tina-sre: quick note — I saw one tenant still getting transient 502s; looks like edge cache not warmed for that tenant. warming cache via admin console (cache:prime tenant=acme-corp).
sam-oncall: cache prime triggered. also toggled fallback TOC to return stale-but-valid org data for 60s for failing lookups.
ryan-eng-runtime: QA: adding an integration test to simulate pool low state; will gate config via rollout with metric checks (error-rate, p99) before full rollout.
maria-cs: CS asking whether we should proactively offer credits for affected calls. filing with billing ops.
sam-oncall: status update for channel: issue detected -> config rollback + CB + cache fallback -> error rate declining -> customer notifications sent -> follow-up PR and capacity runbook. I will remain until error rate <1% for 30m or pass to next oncall.
tina-sre: started postmortem stub: https://docs.internal/incidents/2310001234 — adding timeline and logs.
sam-oncall: handing off to @ryan-eng-runtime for continued monitoring. I'm offline at 11:00.
ryan-eng-runtime: acked takeover. continuing watch and will coordinate the PR and DB runbook with infra. ping me if any regression.
maria-cs: thanks all — CS will follow up with customers with a more detailed root cause and planned remediation timeline. :pray: 
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: error rate returned to baseline; incident marked resolved after 38m. follow-up: postmortem required.
